The misconception likely stems from the use of red cloth (muleta or muleta de muerte) in traditional bullfighting. The red cloth is used to attract the bull's attention and provoke it into charging, but the bull is responding to the movement of the cloth, not its color. In modern bullfighting, the color of the clothing worn by the matador is irrelevant; what matters is the skillful handling of the cape (muleta).

In summary, bulls react to movement, not color, and red clothing is not inherently dangerous around them.
